about: Receipts that test the seed host record rules and the native stage tool rows, judged by both
stage-receipt readers: src/tests/fixed_point.rs runs the Rust reader on every case, and
scripts/tests/stage_receipt_reader_parity_test.py runs scripts/lib/stage_receipt_provenance.py
on the same inputs. Each case starts from `base` (the receipt and files of
reference.json.gz file case `reference_case`), from `fixed-point` (that receipt after the
`fixed_point` edits) or from `native-lld` (that receipt after the `native_lld` edits: the
in-tree LLVM identity reference file case 131 states, with lld's output directory beside
LLVM's, and a rust-lld row bound to it), applies its own `edits` in order, and writes the
result as the stage's tool-provenance.json, beside the reference case's files, the case's
own `files` (a stage-relative path to the hex of its bytes) and its own `links` (a
stage-relative path to the text of a symbolic link: the name of a file in the same
directory, which need not exist). An edit sets or deletes one key
of an existing object; a path beginning with an `@` name continues `paths[name]`, and an
integer in a path is an index of a list. A case either has `lines`, the exact PROVENANCE
lines (`<receipt>` stands for the sha256 of the bytes the reader was given), or `refusal`,
the exact reason (`<toolchain>` stands for the stage directory the reader was given). The
cases port the Python reader's fixed-point tests (scripts/tests/recreate_bootstrap_test.py,
docs/PLAN.md PKG-S6) and the `native_stage_tools` branch of its `_recorded_files`. A case
labelled `first refusal:` holds two faults, each refused alone, and pins which one is named
first.
